sector: Independent continuing professional education institute running a community evening programme and an employer funded executive programme from two campus buildings.
founded_place_size: Founded 1978, two campus buildings in Vermont, cohort run by registrar Helen Abbott.
about: Cedarline teaches working adults across two very different registers: an accessible community evening course and a high cost executive programme bought by employers. Each autumn cohort finishes with a ceremony where every candidate leaves with a certificate in hand and a file in their inbox the same evening. The Institute trades on being trusted rather than flashy, and on the two credentials reading honestly for what they cost.
audience: Community students in their twenties and thirties whose certificate is read by family at home, and executive candidates whose employer funded credential ends up framed in an office where their own clients see it.
price_positioning: Two credentials an order of magnitude apart: a 180 dollar community certificate and a 9,000 dollar employer funded executive credential. Neither can come off the press looking like the other. Cohort run posts around 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.
typography: An engraved, higher contrast serif for the executive register, set with generous margins and the seal given room. A warmer, plainly legible serif for the community certificate. The two share bones but never the same weight or spacing.
voice: Measured and earned, never boastful. We state what was completed and who signed it. Example line the brand would write: 'Completed the autumn programme in professional practice. Signed at Cedarline Institute, Vermont.'
brand_assets_status: The seal die went to the printer that closed and cannot be recovered. The only surviving seal is the one blind embossed into an old certificate, plus a raking light photograph of that impression. Two dead press files remain, last year's community certificate and the 2019 executive diploma; there is no digital seal artwork.
values: Each credential must be honest about its price, and every candidate name spelled and accented correctly right up to the ceremony morning.
